To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

i) PCLC in HPSS were reported higher in rural than urban area, ii) principals in Fully residential secondary school achieved the highest PCLS, followed by principals of Daily Secondary School and religious secondary school, iii) PCLC were reliably related to the types of HPSS, iv) principals of HPBS achieved the highest mean scores of PCLC but lowest score in Defuse Resistance and Conflict domain, regardless of the location and types of HPSS.

(a) the principals in HPSS have adequate PCLC to manage change, but not competent in the Defusing Resistance and Conflicts domain, (b) the PCLC is not reliably related to the location of school, (c) the principals in Fully Residential School achieved the highest mean scores of PCLC, (d) the PCLCs were reliably related to the HPSS, (e) the PCL was reliably related to type of HPSS, and (f
principals in HPSS are competent in the domain Goal Framing but not in the domain of Capacity Building and Defusing Resistance and conflict.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the principal in the management of change in schools.
the question of whether and how the leadership of principals in high performing secondary school (HPSS) is perceived by teachers to be effective.
the development of the principals’ change leadership competencies in Malaysian HPSS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research has shown that the principals of High Performing Secondary School in Malaysia have a good level of competencies in the four domains of Change Leadership Competencies.
this study provides an insight of PCLC and its relationship with school location and type in HPSS.
principals’ PCLC in HPSS was adequate and the findings could be used as a reference for principals to enhance their leadership competency in change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
principals’ competencies to lead change in schools are not merely a matter of individual characteristics.
the findings revealed that principals in Malaysian HPSS possess adequate change leadership competencies.
we have identified a set of competencies for school principals that are necessary for leading change in schools and we have developed and validated a measure of these competencies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a need to improve principals’ capacity in the Defusing Resistance and conflict domain.
principals’ change leadership competencies are essential to the success of school change.
principals in HPSS in Malaysia possess adequate PCLCs in all four domains.
